title: Research: generative-repair agent for poorly reconstructed splat regions (detect, choose a fix, verify)
summary: Research spike, corpus only. Build and evaluate an offline agent that finds the badly reconstructed regions of a room splat and repairs them, keeping only repairs that measurably improve the room against its source frames. Motivation: the Owner's iPhone 14 checks of the Winchester Great Hall splat room (builds 48 and 50, M1-UNITY-01) showed sharp regions where the video looked, and smears, white blown-out blobs and dark shapes near the floor, columns and entrance where it did not. Training-side fixes (antialiased rasterisation, bilateral-grid exposure compensation, scale regularisation, pruning) and camera limits (services/reconstruction/tools/room_limits.py) narrow the problem but cannot invent content the video never saw. (1) Detect: per region (floor grid cell / voxel), score low training-view coverage (frustum counts and viewing-angle spread from the COLMAP poses, as room_limits.py does), splat statistics (opacity and scale variance, needle and giant splats, isolated splats) and render-versus-source error on held-out frames (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS per region). (2) Choose a fix per region, cheapest first: (a) retrain with targeted settings (pose refinement, more iterations, densification limits) or re-extract more frames for that part of the video; (b) diffusion novel-view repair: render pseudo-views from poses interpolated from the training cameras toward the bad region, clean them with a single-step image diffusion fixer conditioned on the nearest real frame, and distil them back into the splat progressively (the Difix3D+ recipe, arXiv 2503.01774); (c) copy from a well-captured duplicate (repeated columns, windows, symmetric walls) found by feature matching or symmetry detection, transformed into place; (d) replace with a clean proxy (textured box/plane or mesh from the collision mesh) or a solid occluder. (3) Verify: every fix is re-scored on held-out source frames and on fixed novel-view probes (no-reference sharpness plus a reviewer pass); a fix that does not improve the region's held-out error, or that worsens any neighbouring region, is reverted. Licence findings so far (web-checked 2026-10-04): Difix3D+ code and the nvidia/difix weights are under the NVIDIA License, whose section 3.3 limits the work and derivatives to non-commercial research or evaluation use, plus the Stability AI Community License for the SD-Turbo base - so Difix may be used to evaluate the approach on the corpus but its outputs must not ship; GSFix3D includes Gaussian-Splatting-licensed code (non-commercial only) and RAIL++-M models; the 3DGS-Enhancer authors have not released the spatial-temporal decoder or confidence-aware 3DGS parts. Shippable path to evaluate: a fixer trained by us with img2img-turbo/pix2pix-turbo (MIT) on SD-Turbo (Stability AI Community License: commercial use allowed below USD 1M annual revenue after registering, outputs owned by us; Enterprise licence above that), with LaMa (Apache-2.0 code and Big-LaMa weights) as a per-view inpainting baseline, and gsplat/nerfstudio (Apache-2.0) for training. Data policy: corpus clips only, no user captures (SECURITY_CHECKLIST 6.3/6.5, AUTH #031, ADR-0005: reconstruction is corpus-only on our own infrastructure; the Owner's own-room capture is covered only by the AUTH REQUEST #046 policy note); generated content is added only to rooms whose source licence allows adaptation (e.g. CC BY with the 'modified' credit already used by the splat room), never to NC/ND or unknown-licence clips; generated regions are recorded per room so they can be flagged or removed. Cost (Modal list prices recorded in M1-RES-01: A10G $1.10/h, L40S $1.95/h, A100 80 GB $2.50/h): measured today, one Winchester retrain with the quality recipe cost $0.60 on an L40S (30k iterations in about 14 min of training, 15 min wall; the two-variant retrain app came to $1.37 on the Modal bill), and it gave a sharper room with fewer floaters but left the out-of-coverage smears that this spike targets; detection is CPU-side (coverage and splat statistics in seconds) plus one held-out render pass; Difix-style repair per room adds pseudo-view fixing (the paper reports 76 ms per single-step fix on an A100; a few hundred to a few thousand fixes per room is minutes of GPU) and one to three progressive retrains, so an estimated $2-6 per room per repair pass on L40S, and $5-15 per room including a failed attempt and verification renders. Training our own fixer: the paper fine-tunes Difix in 'a few hours on a single consumer graphics card'; budget about 10-20 A100-hours ($25-50) for data generation and fine-tuning, plus the pair-generation retrains. Phase 1 (detection + report on 5 corpus rooms, about $10), phase 2 (retrain and proxy fixes with verification, about $25), phase 3 (evaluate Difix3D+ non-commercially on 3 rooms as the quality reference, about $20), phase 4 (train our own MIT/SD-Turbo fixer and compare, about $50-75). Suggested total spend request: $150 for the spike, inside the Modal workspace limit. AUTH spend request note: needs an Owner spend AUTH before any GPU run beyond the M1-UNITY-01 retrain; the AUTH Decisions table entry is the Owner's to write.

acceptance_tests.test: A region report for at least 5 corpus rooms ranks regions by coverage, splat statistics and held-out render error, and its worst regions match the artifacts reviewers mark on fixed probe views (the Winchester floor/column/entrance smears among them).
acceptance_tests.evidence: region_report output + probe renders with marked regions

acceptance_tests.test: For each tried fix type (retrain, diffusion repair, duplicate copy, proxy/occluder) the agent records before/after held-out PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS per region and keeps only fixes that improve the region without worsening neighbours; reverted fixes are listed with the reason.

Licence and data-policy check per component (code, weights, base model, training data) is written up; nothing from a non-commercial-licence model is written into a shippable package, and generated content only enters rooms whose source licence allows adaptation, with the credit marked 'modified'.
acceptance_tests.evidence: research/generative-repair/README.md licence table + package manifest check

acceptance_tests.test: Measured GPU cost per room per fix type (cost.json style: GPU + CPU + memory) is reported against the estimates in this ticket, and total spend stays within the approved AUTH line.

Recommendation: which fix types to automate in the reconstruction pipeline (M1-PIPE-01 / M1-CAPT-03), with expected cost per room and the quality gain on device (an iPhone check of one repaired room).

security: Corpus only; no user imagery (SPEC section 6.3, ADR-0005)

Status -> in-progress, phase 1 (CPU only, $0). Ran services/reconstruction/tools/weak_regions.py on Winchester (the 828,710-splat quality-30k training output, with the shipped 400K prune and the 19 held-out eval views). Results: walk area 58 cells, median 15.3 training views, 1 weak cell (2%); camera box 95 cells, 23% weak, worst in the -x/-z corner behind the spawn toward the entrance (5-7 views, held-out error 0.10-0.23 vs a 0.035 walk-area median); the ring visible from the camera box (within 4 m) is 83% weak (median 2.7 views; 251K splats, 47% of them removed by the display prune). Floor band (<0.4 m) has twice the giant-splat share of the rest (1.05% vs 0.49%) and more needles (3.3% vs 2.5%). Coverage, not trainer settings, is the main cause, so phase 2 should target the visible ring (proxy or occluder plus re-capture) rather than retraining. Summary: qa/evidence/M1-PIPE-02/winchester-weak-regions-phase1.json; map kept on the box (not committed).
